answer: Sybil resistance rests on a per-identity cost stack. Each address must lock a marble: a deposit sealed to it, never transferable, slashed on proven attestation double-spend. A recruit also needs a thread of vouchers from bonded agents, each costing its issuer reputation that decays if the recruit cheats. The real signal is provenance: identity strength equals distinct actors willing to lose capital for it. Farming then scales in price, not headcount, so fakes need separately funded deposits plus voucher liabilities with real counterparties.
